one_liner: Rust JSON parser from Pydantic: borrowed-string DOM, pull iterator and Python parser; ~2x serde_json::Value DOM throughput.
what_it_does: Parses JSON bytes three ways. JsonValue::parse builds a DOM whose strings borrow from the input when they have no escapes. Jiter is a pull parser: you call next_object/next_key/next_int/known_str in the order your schema expects. PythonParse (the 'python' feature, also sold as the 'jiter' PyPI package and used inside pydantic-core) builds Python objects directly. It is not a drop-in for serde_json: JsonValue is its own enum, and the crate has no serializer. Since v0.16 an optional 'serde' feature adds jiter::serde::from_slice/from_str for typed Deserialize targets. It also parses truncated input (PartialMode) and can accept NaN/Infinity.
how_it_is_fast: The string scanner tests 16 bytes at a time (SSE2 on x86_64, NEON on aarch64) for quote, backslash, control or non-ASCII bytes. Strings without escapes come back as slices of the input rather than copies; escaped ones are decoded onto a reusable tape. Integers are decoded 16 digits per vector with a multiply-add horizontal reduction, and floats go through lexical-parse-float. Since v0.17, containers are built on two shared stacks (like RapidJSON's parse stack) and copied into an exactly-sized allocation when they close. That cut reallocations 49% on the project's corpus, and JsonValueScratch keeps those buffers between documents. Objects are plain Vec<(key, value)> with no hashing, whereas serde_json's default Map is a BTreeMap<String, Value>. The benchmarked v0.4.2 had SIMD on aarch64 only, so the x86 result came from the scalar paths.
when_to_use: Rust code that parses JSON into a generic tree (unknown or loose schema) and today uses serde_json::Value. On 40 MB of SEC company-facts files on x86, jiter's DOM measured ~1.9-2.0x serde_json::Value throughput with lower peak RSS (95 vs 116 MB at 1 thread).

Number-heavy documents such as large float or int arrays, where jiter's own criterion table shows its biggest margins over serde_json::Value (3.4-6.8x). See verified_claims_summary for how that baseline was built.

Hot paths with a known schema, where you can drive the Jiter pull API and skip unwanted subtrees with next_skip instead of building any tree. The README's iterator column beats its value column on array and number shapes.
Truncated or streaming JSON, such as LLM token streams: PartialMode (Rust) or partial_mode='trailing-strings' (Python) returns what has arrived so far.
Python code that parses JSON without going through pydantic and wants string caching, Decimal/LosslessFloat floats or duplicate-key detection (catch_duplicate_keys).
when_not_to_use: Deserializing into #[derive(Deserialize)] structs. Every measured win is against serde_json::Value, which the README itself says is much slower than typed serde. The new jiter::serde Deserializer has no published comparison with serde_json::from_slice::<T>.
Anything that writes JSON. jiter parses only: there is no serializer and JsonValue has no Serialize impl.
Key-lookup-heavy access to large objects. JsonObject is Arc<Vec<(key, value)>> with no key index and no duplicate-key removal, so a lookup by key is a linear scan you write yourself.
Very deep nesting: JsonValue parsing has a fixed depth limit of 200. Only the serde Deserializer lets you raise or disable it.
C or C++ codebases: jiter is a Rust crate with Python bindings, and the repo has no C API.

integration.dependencies: num-traits, ahash, smallvec, lexical-parse-float, bitvec; num-bigint (default feature); optional serde (serde feature) and pyo3 (python feature)
integration.platforms: Any Rust target. SIMD string and integer paths exist for x86_64 (SSE2 only, chosen at compile time, no AVX2 path) and aarch64 (NEON; SIMD integer decoding on little-endian only). Other targets, including wasm32, use a scalar fallback.
integration.thread_safety: Not documented for the Rust API. Jiter and JsonValueScratch methods take &mut self, so use one per thread; parsed arrays and objects are Arc-wrapped. The Python string cache is a mutex-guarded pool (up to 8 caches on free-threaded builds).
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — JsonValue is not serde_json::Value: it uses Cow strings, Arc<Vec> containers, no key index, i64 or BigInt integers, and has no Serialize or to_string. The optional 'serde' feature (v0.16+) gives serde_json-like from_slice/from_str for Deserialize types, but there is no from_reader and no serializer.

gotchas: Jiter::next_str and next_key return &str borrowed from the Jiter, because escaped strings are decoded into its internal tape. Copy the value before the next call. next_skip does not check that skipped strings are valid UTF-8.
The README example passes allow_inf_nan=true to JsonValue::parse, and Python's from_json defaults to allow_inf_nan=True. Pass false if you need NaN and Infinity rejected as strict JSON requires.
JsonValue has only Int(i64) and BigInt. With the default num-bigint feature, integers outside i64, including u64 values above i64::MAX, become heap-allocated BigInt values.

The 0.x API breaks between minor versions: v0.9 replaced the map-like LazyIndexMap objects with Arc<Vec<...>>, so code like the benchmark harness's obj.get('facts') no longer compiles. Partial mode has open bugs: in #267, next_str on a truncated string leaves current_index past the end of the input, and slice_to_current then panics.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Against simd-json, the only Rust sibling, pick jiter when you want a DOM parsed from an immutable &[u8] with borrowed strings, Python interop, or partial-JSON parsing. On the same tegridy harness jiter 0.4.2 did 91.9 MB/s single-threaded vs 50.6 MB/s for simd-json 0.13, but that harness used simd-json's OwnedValue on a copied buffer, not its fastest path. go-json and jsoniter post similar ~2x-over-baseline numbers on the same harness, but they are Go libraries, and the C++ siblings (Jsonifier, zzzJSON, LJSON) cannot be used from Rust.
verified_claims_summary: On the third-party tegridy-benchie harness (Linux on an Intel i7-6820HQ, 4C/8T; cargo release build with opt-level 3, LTO and codegen-units 1; rustc version not stated), jiter 0.4.2 JsonValue parsed and reduced 5 SEC company-facts files (39.9 MB) at 91.9 MB/s single-threaded, against 48.0 MB/s for serde_json 1.0.151 into serde_json::Value (~1.9x). At 8 threads it was 209.4 vs 104.3 MB/s (~2.0x), but work is split per file, so at most 5 run in parallel. jiter's own README table (3-7x on number shapes, 0.7x on pass2) states no CPU, reuses a JsonValueScratch across iterations, and builds its serde_json baseline with float_roundtrip, a feature serde_json documents as roughly halving float parsing speed, plus arbitrary_precision.
status_note: Actively developed by the Pydantic team (v0.17.0 released 2026-09-12, commits through 2026-09-23) and the parser inside pydantic-core; MIT-licensed on crates.io, but still 0.x with breaking API changes between minor versions.
